params.why: keep the sample space small for the entry-point tier

params.name: onlyA
params.let: sorted([P[i] for i in range(0, total) if i < na])

params.name: both
params.let: sorted([P[i] for i in range(0, total) if i >= na and i < na + nab])

params.name: onlyB
params.let: sorted([P[i] for i in range(0, total) if i >= na + nab and i < na + nab + nb])

params.name: neither
params.let: sorted([P[i] for i in range(0, total) if i >= na + nab + nb])

params.name: evA
params.let: sorted([P[i] for i in range(0, total) if i < na + nab])

params.name: evB
params.let: sorted([P[i] for i in range(0, total) if i >= na and i < na + nab + nb])

params.name: outA
params.let: sorted([P[i] for i in range(0, total) if i >= na + nab])

constraints: len(onlyA) > 0 and len(both) > 0 and len(onlyB) > 0 and len(neither) > 0
stem: A Venn diagram shows the sample space $S = \{n : n \in \mathbb{Z}, 1 \leq n \leq {=total}\}$. Two circles, one for the event $A$ and one for the event $B$, overlap inside the rectangle $S$. The numbers of $S$ are placed in the diagram as follows. Inside circle $A$ only: ${=setof(onlyA)}$. Inside both circles, in the overlap: ${=setof(both)}$. Inside circle $B$ only: ${=setof(onlyB)}$. Outside both circles: ${=setof(neither)}$. Which of the following sets is the event set of $A$?
solution: The event set of $A$ is made of every number that lies inside circle $A$. Circle $A$ includes the part where it overlaps circle $B$, because the numbers there are inside both circles.
Inside circle $A$ only: ${=setof(onlyA)}$. In the overlap, which is also inside circle $A$: ${=setof(both)}$.
Put the two parts together: the event set of $A$ is ${=setof(evA)}$.
The other sets each read the diagram wrongly: ${=setof(both)}$ is only the overlap, ${=setof(evB)}$ is everything inside circle $B$, and ${=setof(outA)}$ is the numbers outside circle $A$.
notes: Entry-point version of the book's ex14-3-2: a small sample space (7 to 10 numbers) and always the event A. Families carry no image, so the Venn diagram is given as its four regions in words (inside A only, in the overlap, inside B only, outside both); the skill kept is reading the circle of A as its own region PLUS the shared overlap. Numbers are shuffled into the four regions by position in a shuffled list, so the regions are disjoint and together cover 1..total. All four regions are non-empty (constraint), which makes the four options provably distinct: correct = A-only plus overlap; distractors = overlap only (mc reads-only-the-overlap), the circle of B (mc reads-the-other-circle), and everything outside circle A = B-only plus neither (mc reads-outside-the-circle, matching the book's {3, 8, 12} distractor). Sets are passed to setof already sorted; if setof does not return bare LaTeX braces, the three {=setof(...)} holes in each template need the reviewer's attention. Simulated 20000 draws offline: options always distinct, correct set always equals A-only union overlap.
